details: archive_mode = off (set in default) on a primary. Without archived WAL there is no point-in-time recovery: the only recoverable states are whatever full backups exist, and every transaction since the newest one is unrecoverable. wal_level = replica, cluster size 168 MB, WAL generated since the last checkpoint statistics reset is visible in PG-INFO-008. A pg_dump is a logical export, not PITR.
title: No WAL archiving: point-in-time recovery impossible

details: Sequence triage_fixture.nearly_full_id_seq is at 2,100,000,000 of an effective maximum of 2,147,483,647 (97.8%, threshold 90%). It backs triage_fixture.nearly_full.id of type int4, whose maximum (2,147,483,647) is not lower than the sequence's own max_value (2,147,483,647). When it runs out, every INSERT that calls nextval fails: "nextval: reached maximum value of sequence" or, if the column type is the binding limit, "integer out of range". Widening the column to bigint rewrites the whole table and every index on it, which is why this is worth seeing at 70% rather than at 99%.
title: Sequence or integer key at 90 percent or more of its range

details: shared_buffers = 128 MB (threshold 128 MB), source configuration file. The shipped default is chosen so the server starts on any machine, not so it performs on this one. This cluster holds 168 MB of data, so at 128 MB the buffer cache can hold 76.2% of it and almost every read goes to the operating-system cache or the disk. effective_cache_size = 4GB. Changing shared_buffers requires a restart.
title: shared_buffers at the shipped default

details: data_checksums = off. Pages carry no checksum, so storage-level corruption is detected only when it happens to break a structure Postgres validates: a torn page, a flipped bit inside a value, or a silently truncated read returns wrong answers instead of an error. Cluster holds 168 MB across 3 databases. Enabling requires pg_checksums with the cluster shut down (PostgreSQL 12 and newer) or a dump and reload. full_page_writes = on.
title: Data checksums disabled

details: max_slot_wal_keep_size = -1 (unlimited) while 1 replication slot(s) exist: triage_fixture_dead_slot (physical, active=f). Any consumer that stops - a crashed logical decoder, a decommissioned standby whose slot was never dropped, a paused CDC connector - pins WAL indefinitely, and pg_wal grows until the volume fills and the primary PANICs. Setting a cap sized to the WAL volume converts that outage into a broken slot (wal_status = lost, PG-REPL-005), which is recoverable. pg_wal currently holds 416 MB.

details: idle_in_transaction_session_timeout = 0 at server level with no role or database override for it. Nothing stops a client that opened a transaction and then went away - a paused debugger, a crashed worker, a connection a firewall silently dropped - from holding its locks and the cluster's xmin horizon indefinitely (PG-LOCK-003, PG-VAC-005). 0 session(s) are in an idle-in-transaction state right now, the oldest for n/a. 5 to 15 minutes for application roles is a common setting; leave interactive and migration roles alone.
title: idle_in_transaction_session_timeout disabled

details: effective_cache_size is at the default 4096 MB with source default. This setting allocates no memory: it tells the planner how much of the data it can expect to find cached, in shared_buffers plus the operating-system page cache. Left at 4 GB on a host with more memory than that, the planner over-estimates the cost of repeated index lookups and drifts towards sequential scans and hash joins. The usual starting point is 50 to 75 percent of RAM. shared_buffers = 128MB, cluster size 168 MB.
title: effective_cache_size at the default

details: temp_file_limit = -1 (unlimited), source default. A single sort, hash join or CTE materialisation that under-estimates its input can write until the data volume is full, at which point every write in the cluster fails and, if pg_wal shares the volume, the server PANICs. The cluster already writes 914 MB of temporary files per day (PG-CAP-008 measures it). A limit sized so one query cannot fill the volume turns that outage into one failed query with "temporary file size exceeds temp_file_limit". work_mem = 4MB.
title: temp_file_limit unlimited

details: log_min_duration_statement = -1 (source default) and auto_explain is not loaded. No statement is ever logged for being slow, so when someone reports that "the application was slow at 3am" there is nothing on the server to look at afterwards: pg_stat_statements (installed here) gives cumulative totals, not the individual slow execution, its parameters or its timestamp. A threshold of 250 to 1000 ms costs one log line per slow statement; on a busy server log_min_duration_sample plus log_statement_sample_rate (PostgreSQL 13 and newer) bound the volume. log_statement = none, log_destination = stderr.
title: Slow-query logging disabled

details: PUBLIC holds CREATE on schema public in database triage_test, so every role that can connect can create objects there. Combined with a search_path that puts public before pg_catalog - which is the default - any such role can define a function or operator that shadows a built-in one and have it executed by other users, including superusers. That is CVE-2018-1058. PostgreSQL 15 removed this grant for new databases; a database created earlier, or restored from an earlier dump, keeps it. Current ACL on schema public: pg_database_owner=UC/pg_database_owner, =UC/pg_database_owner. Roles that can log in: 1.
title: PUBLIC can CREATE in schema public

details: Function triage_fixture.unsafe_definer(p integer) is SECURITY DEFINER, owned by postgres, written in sql, with no search_path pinned in its configuration. It runs with the owner's privileges but resolves unqualified names using the caller's search_path, so a caller who can create objects in any schema on that path (see PG-SEC-013) can substitute their own function, operator or table and have the owner execute it. Fix: ALTER FUNCTION triage_fixture.unsafe_definer(p integer) SET search_path = pg_catalog, <the schemas it needs>. EXECUTE is granted to: PUBLIC (default grant).
title: SECURITY DEFINER functions without a fixed search_path

details: lock_timeout = 0 at server level. A statement that needs a lock waits for it forever - and while an ALTER TABLE waits for its ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, every subsequent statement against the same table queues behind the waiting ALTER, including plain SELECTs. That is how a routine migration behind one long transaction (PG-LOCK-005) becomes a total outage on a hot table. Setting lock_timeout to a few seconds in migration sessions makes the migration fail instead of the application. statement_timeout = 10s, deadlock_timeout = 1s, log_lock_waits = off.
title: lock_timeout unset

details: random_page_cost = 4 (the default), seq_page_cost = 1, with baseline.storage = nvme. The 4:1 ratio models a spinning disk where a random seek costs four sequential reads. On SSD, NVMe and cloud block storage the real ratio is close to 1, and leaving it at 4 makes the planner prefer sequential scans over index scans on exactly the queries where an index would win. 1.1 for local NVMe and 1.1 to 2.0 for cloud volumes are the common settings.
title: random_page_cost at the spinning-disk default
